plates.name: the plates
examine: A stack of plates, balanced. I can feel every one of them.

say.text: I scrape the napkins and the bits into the bin, quietly, so as not to put her off.
The top plate has stuck to my jumper. Sweet chilli.
I peel it off. It pulls at the wool.
A dark, sticky mark on my sweater. It'll stay.

useText: I can't put them down here.

objects.name: the shrine
objects.examine: A shelf with a photograph and two oranges. The incense is still going.

objects.name: the calendar
objects.examine: A calendar. Every day on it has been crossed off, including the ones that haven't happened.

objects.name: the drawing
objects.examine: A child's drawing of the family. There's one more person in it than at the table.

objects.name: the rice cooker
objects.examine: The rice cooker. Its light says KEEP WARM. It always has.

objects.name: the fridge
objects.examine: A fridge with every school report on it, held up by magnets from places nobody's been.

objects.name: the television
objects.examine: The television's on with the sound down. Someone on it is also having dinner.

objects.name: the dumplings
examine: Dumplings. The steamer is never empty.
We ate so many. We eat more.

objects.name: the street door
objects.examine: Frosted glass. The street outside is the wrong street.

objects.name: the sign
objects.examine: The company name on the door, backwards from in here. My grandfather, my father, his brother. And sons.

objects.name: the window
examine: The street. A lamp, the block opposite, nobody.
The blinds were always like that. Nobody ever straightened them.

objects.name: the telephone

objects.name: the water cooler
objects.examine: The water cooler. A bubble goes up it now and then, like a thought.

objects.name: the clock
objects.examine: The clock. It's eight in the evening and quarter past four at once.

objects.name: the notice board
objects.examine: A notice board. Memos from a year that didn't have this many months.

objects.name: the bin
examine: A big bin. The office kind, with a bag in it.
Half full of other people's dinners.

lines.text: Hang on, I've nearly got the bridge.
«Doorstop.» You hold the door for me. «Doorstop.» You hold the door, you see.
What do you think? It's for Bladerunner. The musical.

variants.text: Too many doors? There's a lot of doors in Bladerunner. Think about it.
Replicant, doorstop. It's nearly a rhyme.
Sorry, I'm rehearsing. Don't mind me.
It's for Bladerunner. The musical. I'm writing it.
Go round me. I'll keep it down.

say.text: Dinner with a family. Dumplings, in steamers, in stacks.
We ate so many.
I want to give something back.
The plates.
Not all of them. Not down the stairs.
I really can carry them.
I'm good at this. I didn't know I was good at this.
He is, look.
The plates are sticky. Every one of them.
Sweet chilli, plum, something darker.
The building has become my father's office.
The company he owned with his brother and my grandfather. I come here in dreams. It stands in for places.
«Doorstop», you hold the door for me...
A woman, late twenties, on a desk, with a guitar.
She's good. She's very pretty, and she's good.
«Doorstop.» Hold the door for me, «doorstop.»
Hold it open and I'll see. «Doorstop.»
Doorstop, with doorstop.
That's lazy.
And it's too much about doors. About what doors do. For Bladerunner.
I don't say anything. There's sauce on my jumper.
«Doorstop...»
